//: package.json is strict JSON and cannot take real comments, so these "//" keys are the convention instead. npm ignores them and preserves them through installs. Real comments ARE allowed in tsconfig.json.
name: search-engine
description: small search engine that will crawl the internet, index files, and rank files to be return by a search interface
//type: ESM, chosen deliberately over commonjs. Means import/export instead of require, and allows top-level await. tsconfig's "module": "nodenext" reads THIS field to decide how to treat .ts files, so the two stay in sync.
//main: Inert. This field only matters for packages that other code imports, and nothing imports this project. Safe to delete. Do NOT change it to .ts — a consumer's Node could not read TypeScript.
//scripts: Each value is a string handed to the shell when you run `npm run <name>`. npm puts node_modules/.bin on PATH first, so bare `tsx` and `tsc` resolve to the local copies. Names here are mine to invent; top-level keys in this file are npm's fixed vocabulary.
//devDependencies: Build-time tools only — nothing here is imported by the running program, so a deployment could skip them. better-sqlite3 will go in "dependencies" instead, since the crawler genuinely imports it. The caret in ^7.0.2 means >=7.0.2 and <8.0.0: minor and patch updates allowed, major held back because that is where breaking changes live.
